title: mcp: record tools name the same thing differently (create returns id, update/get/delete take recordId; query takes where), and the unknown-key refusal cites retired keys
body:
Filing category: ① product defect.
reach: public entry `/api/v1/mcp` `tools/call`, measured once on `objectos-ee` (cloud `ff373e02`, framework `d7c3d44e`).
Batch-of: 15 cards filed together from one MCP capability test session (2026-11-11; 6 in cloud, 9 in objectstack).

## Business reason

An agent chains `create_record` → `update_record` → `get_record`; each name mismatch costs a refused call. The refusal text then sends it to a protocol-upgrade guide that has nothing to do with its mistake.

## What happens

1. `create_record` answers `{ object, id, record }`; `update_record`, `get_record`, `delete_record` require `recordId`. An agent passing `id` gets: `Invalid arguments for tool update_record: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined at recordId / Unrecognized key(s) on this update_record call: id. Did you mean id → recordId? Keys retired before the previous protocol major are no longer prescribed here — see the protocol upgrade guide: https://objectstack.ai/docs/protocol-upgrade.`
2. `query_records` takes `where`; passing `filter` (the word most clients use) gets the same "Keys retired before the previous protocol major … protocol upgrade guide" sentence. Same for `list_objects({ includeSystem: true })`.
3. The appended sentence comes from `packages/spec/src/shared/protocol-upgrade-guide.ts` and is added to every unknown-key refusal, including keys that were never part of any protocol.

## Expected

One spelling for the record id across the record tools (the answer of `create_record` and the argument of the others agree), and the unknown-key refusal names the right key without the retired-key/upgrade-guide sentence when the key was never retired.

Reader who acts: the seat that owns `packages/mcp` tool schemas (and `packages/spec` for the shared refusal sentence).
Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue recordId mcp update_record id` → 27 hits; top 3 (#30223, #29050, #28106) are chat/automation, none on MCP argument naming.
